A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching core SCO results, constructions, and proofs. The text, equations, table, figure, and complete appendices support comparison despite the changed title and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 presents theoretical bounds, mathematical constructions, and proofs. Its schematic and summary table contain no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: V2 remains theoretical throughout its main text and appendices. The added mean-estimation corollary and ERM analysis are mathematical results, not empirical evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix F.5 adds a theoretical estimator-to-SCO reduction: a mean estimate is mapped to the parameter maximizing its inner product over the feasible set, allowing application of existing tracing results. The original SCO constructions and tracing procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or tasks in empirical training or evaluation. The added mean-estimation setting is a theoretical extension, rather than new evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates baseline methods experimentally. The expanded comparison with DSSUV15 and BST14 concerns mathematical techniques and guarantees.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental splits, budgets, model configurations, or testing procedures. The illustrative change from epsilon = 0.1 to 0.01 concerns theoretical DP risk definitions, not an evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests, or error analyses. The added analysis in Appendix B.1 is a mathematical derivation, assessed under T1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probabilistic guarantees concern theoretical tracing bounds rather than empirical uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: No measured scores, experimental rankings, or empirical findings are added or revised. Table 1 retains the same asymptotic rates; additions to theoretical results are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: V2 adds Corollary 2.9 and its Appendix F.5 proof, extending Omega(log(d)/alpha^2) traceability to infinity-norm mean estimation, plus the ERM derivation in Appendix B.1. Definition 3.2 also removes tracer convexity, substantively broadening the formal trace-value class, although retained polytope arguments still require it. V1's explicit conjectured optimal rate for p > 2 is deleted. The principal SCO bounds and fingerprinting proofs otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The central SCO traceability and DP lower-bound claims remain. V2 adds an explicit contribution claiming closure of the log(d) traceability gap for infinity-norm mean estimation and emphasizes dimension-dependent recall in the introduction and Corollary 2.9.

C2.justification: V2 removes Section 3.4's conjecture about optimal DP-SCO rates for p > 2 and its discussion of what resolving it would imply, while retaining the acknowledgment that the optimal rate is unknown. It also removes the explicit explanation for excluding p = infinity because private and non-private risks are comparable.

D1.justification: Neither version provides implementation hyperparameters, hardware specifications, code releases, or empirical reproduction instructions. The retained distribution-sampling descriptions and construction parameters serve mathematical proofs.

R1.justification: DSSUV15 and ADHLR24 remain the closest antecedents. V2 expands the comparison with DSSUV15/BST14, explicitly acknowledges the tracing–DP connection from FS17 in the main text, and adds BMNSY18, XR17, and LT24. Several nearest-neighbor, benign-overfitting, and fingerprinting-history citations are removed.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the title, extensively rewrites the abstract and introduction around traceability, reorders the geometry-specific contributions, and adds a technical-contributions subsection. Much related work moves to Appendix B, and the scaling-matrix fingerprinting lemma moves from the main text to Appendix D.2.

P2.justification: V1's risk-regime schematic, Figure 1, is removed. Table 1 retains its content and structure but moves from page 5 to page 4. Several displayed definitions and equations become more compact, while the basic single-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: The mean-estimation corollary and expanded comparison with prior techniques add useful scope and explanation. However, unlike v1, v2 drops tracer convexity from Definition 3.2 while retained arguments still require it, notably Theorem E.6 and Proposition G.3. This unresolved inconsistency in the formal framework creates a material tradeoff with the additions and clearer exposition, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
